decisive_items: Revealed epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
response.rationale: R2 is supported by classic pemphigus vulgaris histology (suprabasal acantholysis), intercellular IgG/C3 on DIF, and elevated anti-desmoglein 1/3 antibodies. R1 lacks specific evidence; Crohn disease alone does not establish paraneoplastic pemphigus, and no neoplasm is mentioned.

rejected.why: No evidence of underlying malignancy or characteristic paraneoplastic pemphigus features; only Crohn history and stoma lesion are nonspecific.
